$comment: The curated table of PUBLIC live cameras for the live demo.
Every row is a real camera, run by somebody else, published publicly on YouTube.
That is what `public relay` means and it is the only claim any row makes: the
camera exists, it is live, and it is NOT ours. `internal/source` derives the
source sentence from that flag - 'public relay of a real camera, NOT ours' - and
no row here turns it into 'live camera'.
WHAT A ROW IS NOT. It is not permission to record. `licence` records the PUBLIC
basis for watching the feed, which is that the operator published it for exactly
that; storing clips is a different act and is the operator's to permit, which is
why `SP_POC_SOURCE_LICENCE` is a required variable for every live source and why
every row below says in words that no written permission to store or republish
has been obtained. A run over these cameras records clips on THIS machine, and
`cleared_for_external_use: false` says a screenshot of the demo is a screenshot
of the camera, which it is.
A camera with no row here is not thereby forbidden: add one, resolve it live,
record what the resolver returned and what ffprobe read, and the run will use
it. What is refused is the alternative - a URL with no row, which is a camera
with no recorded basis and no date anybody checked it.

cameras.name: EarthCam Live: Times Square North 4K
cameras.place: Times Square, Manhattan, New York City, USA
cameras.licence: EarthCam publishes this camera publicly on YouTube for viewing, and watching the feed is public. No written permission to store or republish clips has been obtained: the footage is EarthCam's and their published terms govern. The basis for a recorded run is whatever SP_POC_SOURCE_LICENCE states, and the clips stay on this machine.
cameras.contains_people: yes - a public square. People are the subject of the view, so a clip from it is personal data and is treated as such.
notes: Resolved live on 2026-10-14 with `yt-dlp --js-runtimes node -g -f bestvideo` to an
HLS playlist on manifest.googlevideo.com, and read by ffprobe: h264, 1920x1080,
30 fps, live. That is the whole content of `verified`: a human ran it, on that
date, and the stream answered.
Chosen for the demo because a busy public square produces the two things the
pipeline is measured on - pedestrians and vehicles - continuously, in daylight
and at night, without anybody staging anything.

cameras.licence: EarthCam publishes this camera publicly on YouTube for viewing, and watching the feed is public. The basis for a recorded run is whatever SP_POC_SOURCE_LICENCE states, and the clips stay on this machine.
cameras.contains_people: yes - a pedestrian crossing, which is the entire subject of the view.
notes: Resolved live on 2026-10-14 to an HLS playlist on manifest.googlevideo.com and
read by ffprobe. Same procedure, same date, same result as the row above.
The second camera because the demo shows at least two real tiles, and because a
zebra crossing is the clearest possible subject for the line-crossing and
presence modes: the line is somewhere a person really does cross.

Held as the third tile and as the fallback when one of the others is between
streams: a row that resolved on the verification date is a row that resolved
THEN, and the resolver's own error names which camera did not answer today.

The fourth tile. Four rather than two, so the demo survives one camera being
offline on the day: the run's first job is to prove the source line, and a
four-row table with one camera down still proves it.
